data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'melikos', which means 'mild' or 'gentle'. In the Bible, Milka is mentioned as the daughter of Abraham and Keturah, and the mother of the sons Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The name Milka carries the meaning “Mild, gentle” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Milka usually hope their child will grow to embody mild, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
